canonical_question: Does the 100- to 650-kHz frequency sweep range fully capture all necessary eigenmodes for NbTaTiV, or could higher-order modes required for accurate inversion be outside this band?

question_variants.question: Does the 100- to 650-kHz frequency sweep range fully capture all necessary eigenmodes for NbTaTiV, or could higher-order modes required for accurate inversion be outside this band?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text specifies a frequency sweep of 100-650 kHz but does not confirm if this range captures all necessary eigenmodes for NbTaTiV inversion.

answers.answer: The frequency was swept through the 100- to 650-kHz range with large responses detected, but the sufficiency of this range for all eigenmodes is not stated.
answers.measurement_outcome: Responses detected at eigenfrequencies within 100-650 kHz
answers.boundary_limitation: No confirmation of higher-order mode coverage outside this band.
evidence_spans: The microstructure of the homogenized NbTaTiV refractory HEA was characterized, using the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) backscattered electron (BSE) technique, as shown in Fig. 1A . A typical simple solid-solution HEA microstructure with grain sizes of 200 to 400 μm was identified without the presence of secondary phases or elemental segregations.

The chemical composition of the sample was verified (using the point energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy analysis) to be Nb 23.8 Ta 25.5 Ti 24.9 V 25.8 , indicating a homogeneous elemental distribution in a nearly equiatomic percentage.
The measured ND patterns of the bulk samples, as illustrated in Fig. 1B , confirm the single BCC solid solution at RT and elevated temperatures.
